definition: Implied volatility is the volatility input that, when plugged into an option pricing model like Black-Scholes, reproduces the option's observed market price.
core_idea: Because volatility can't be directly observed (unlike rates, prices, strikes, and expirations), it's backed out by iteratively guessing a volatility value, computing the model price, and comparing to the actual traded price until the two match.
key_points: All other Black-Scholes inputs are observable or easily estimated from the market or contract terms.
Volatility is the one input that must be inferred rather than observed.
The standard method is numerical: guess sigma, solve Black-Scholes, compare to market price, and refine the guess iteratively.
trading_implications: Traders quote and trade options in terms of implied volatility rather than dollar premium in many markets.
